paper_title: One Tokenizer To Rule Them All Emergent Language Plasticity via   Multilingual Tokenizers
caption: : Effect of vocabulary size.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates how accuracy changes with different vocabulary sizes for two tokenizer settings, shown as two lines with distinct markers and colors. The x-axis is labeled with vocabulary size values “100k,” “175k,” and “250k” on a linear scale, spanning from 100k to 250k with tick marks at each of the three values. The y-axis is labeled “Accuracy (%)” on a linear scale, ranging from 40.5 to 42.0 with evenly spaced tick labels every 0.5 (40.5, 41.0, 41.5, 42.0). One line represents the “universal” tokenizer, drawn in blue with a solid line and star markers; it increases across the x-axis from about 40.45% at 100k to about 41.15% at 175k and about 41.85% at 250k. The other line represents the “cluster” tokenizer, drawn in orange with a solid line and circular markers; it is about 41.62% at 100k, rises to about 41.78% at 175k, and then drops to about 41.42% at 250k. A legend titled “Tokenizer” in the lower-right maps the blue star line to “universal” and the orange circle line to “cluster.”
